outputs.description: Read pairs in, mates merged, reads discarded and sequences retained, from an AdapterRemoval .settings report. The counts balance exactly, which is what lets a read-fate flow be drawn from them without apportioning anything. One row per report, so a pipeline that trims per lane gets one row per lane.
outputs.name: Trimming and collapsing statistics

outputs.description: One row per sequence cluster AMPcombi built across the run with MMseqs2, with the representative sequence header, the sample that contributed it and the number of members.
outputs.name: Peptide clusters

outputs.name: Property embedding
outputs.rawYaml:
id: ampcombi_embedding
name: Property embedding
mode: amp/embedding
description: >-
  Two-dimensional PCA of the AMP candidates over their physicochemical
  descriptors (molecular weight, isoelectric point, hydrophobicity and the
  helix, turn and sheet fractions), standardised before the decomposition.
find: { path_glob: "**/ampcombi2/Ampcombi_summary.tsv" }
recipe: ampcombi/embedding.py
fixture: embedding.tsv
renders_as:
  # One point per candidate, so the embedding's `sample_id` role carries the
  # CDS id. Charge class is the default colour because the plane is a
  # physicochemical one; the sample and the per-tool probabilities ride along in
  # the output, and the renderer's colour menu reaches them.
  - { id: amp_embedding, component: advanced_viz, kind: embedding, roles: {sample_id: cds_id, dim_1: dim_1, dim_2: dim_2, color: charge_class} }
  - { component: table }

outputs.name: AMP candidates
outputs.rawYaml:
id: ampcombi_summary
name: AMP candidates
mode: amp/candidates
description: >-
  One row per antimicrobial-peptide candidate, with the per-tool probabilities,
  the physicochemistry AMPcombi computes (molecular weight, isoelectric point,
  hydrophobicity, secondary-structure fractions) and the reference-database hit.
find: { path_glob: "**/ampcombi2/Ampcombi_summary.tsv" }
recipe: ampcombi/summary.py
fixture: summary.tsv
renders_as:
  # The same property plane as a first-class kind rather than hand-drawn code.
  # AMPcombi computes no net charge at pH 7, so the isoelectric point is the
  # charge axis it actually reports: above about 7 the peptide is cationic at
  # physiological pH, which with a high hydrophobicity is the classic
  # membrane-active shape. Colour is the binned charge class so the three
  # families stay separable, size the peptide length.
  - id: amp_property_scatter
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: scatter_xy
    roles: {x: hydrophobicity, y: isoelectric_point, label: cds_id, color: charge_class, size: aa_length}
  # Charge against hydrophobicity is the classic AMP property plane: cationic
  # and hydrophobic peptides cluster in the upper right. Colour = best tool
  # probability, size = peptide length.
  - component: figure
    code: |
      # keep the physicochemistry complete so no point is silently dropped
      df_modified = df.drop_nulls(["hydrophobicity", "isoelectric_point", "prob_max"])

      fig = px.scatter(
          df_modified.to_pandas(),
          x="hydrophobicity",
          y="isoelectric_point",
          color="prob_max",
          size="aa_length",
          size_max=18,
          opacity=0.75,
          color_continuous_scale="Tealgrn",
          hover_name="cds_id",
          custom_data=["sample"],
      )
      fig.update_layout(
          xaxis_title="Hydrophobicity",
          yaxis_title="Isoelectric point (pI)",
          coloraxis_colorbar_title="Best probability",
          margin={"t": 24, "l": 56, "r": 16, "b": 48},
      )
  - { component: card, column: cds_id, aggregation: count, secondary_layout: donut, breakdown_col: charge_class }
  - { component: card, column: prob_ampir, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: aa_length, aggregation: average, secondary_layout: histogram }
  - { component: card, column: prob_max, aggregation: average, secondary_layout: threshold, threshold_value: 0.8, threshold_direction: min, threshold_warn: 0.6 }
  - { component: table, row_selection_enabled: true, row_selection_column: cds_id }

renders_as.code:
# keep the physicochemistry complete so no point is silently dropped
df_modified = df.drop_nulls(["hydrophobicity", "isoelectric_point", "prob_max"])

fig = px.scatter(
    df_modified.to_pandas(),
    x="hydrophobicity",
    y="isoelectric_point",
    color="prob_max",
    size="aa_length",
    size_max=18,
    opacity=0.75,
    color_continuous_scale="Tealgrn",
    hover_name="cds_id",
    custom_data=["sample"],
)
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Hydrophobicity",

outputs.description: The distribution blocks of `bcftools stats`, melted into one long frame so a single `section` filter drives every tile instead of five separate collections. `section` is one of `indel_length` (insertion and deletion length, deletions negative), `substitution` (the A to C, A to G, ... substitution spectrum), `depth` (read depth), `allele_frequency` (non-reference allele frequency) and `singleton_stats` (variants seen in exactly one allele copy). The key column differs per section, which is the price of melting: a numeric distribution puts its x value in `bin` and leaves `label` null, a categorical one puts its x value in `label` and leaves `bin` null, and `depth` fills both because bcftools writes its open-ended top bucket under a non-numeric bin name. `count` is always a count of variant records, but of a different kind per section (sites for indel length and depth, SNPs for allele frequency, substitutions or singletons for the two categorical ones), so summing it within a filtered section is meaningful and summing it across sections is not. Sample and caller are read off the report's own `ID` line, so any layout a pipeline publishes the reports under works. The quality block is left out: it is most of the rows of a real callset, and the VCFtools Ts/Tv-by-quality sweep answers its question.

outputs.name: Variant distributions per caller
outputs.rawYaml:
id: bcftools_stats_sections
name: Variant distributions per caller
mode: stats-sections
description: >-
  The distribution blocks of `bcftools stats`, melted into one long frame so
  a single `section` filter drives every tile instead of five separate
  collections. `section` is one of `indel_length` (insertion and
  deletion length, deletions negative), `substitution` (the A to C, A to G,
  ... substitution spectrum), `depth` (read depth), `allele_frequency` (non-reference allele frequency) and
  `singleton_stats` (variants seen in exactly one allele copy). The key
  column differs per section, which is the price of melting: a numeric
  distribution puts its x value in `bin` and leaves `label` null, a
  categorical one puts its x value in `label` and leaves `bin` null, and
  `depth` fills both because bcftools writes its open-ended top bucket under
  a non-numeric bin name. `count` is always a count of variant records, but
  of a different kind per section (sites for indel length and depth, SNPs
  for allele frequency, substitutions or singletons for the two
  categorical ones), so summing it within a filtered section is meaningful
  and summing it across sections is not. Sample and caller are read off the
  report's own `ID` line, so any layout a pipeline publishes the reports
  under works. The quality block is left out: it is most of the rows of a
  real callset, and the VCFtools Ts/Tv-by-quality sweep answers its question.
find:
  path_glob: "**/*.bcftools_stats.txt"
recipe: bcftools/stats_sections.py
fixture: stats_sections.tsv
renders_as:
  - { component: figure, visu_type: bar, dict_kwargs: {x: bin, y: count, color: caller} }
  # Which distribution a filtered view is looking at, and how the total
  # splits across the sections still in scope.
  - { component: card, column: count, aggregation: sum, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: section, top_n_count: 3 }
  - { component: table }

mode: summary
description: >-

  file a methylseq run publishes that puts the read funnel and the cytosine
  counts side by side. Adds the ratios a reader asks of those counts: alignment
  and duplication yields, methylation level per context, and the bisulfite

recipe: bismark/summary_report.py

renders_as:

  # survived deduplication, how many CpG calls came out the far end.

outputs.name: BGC region coordinates
outputs.rawYaml:
id: combgc_region_track
name: BGC region coordinates
mode: bgc/track
description: >-
  The comBGC regions as coordinates rather than counts: contig, interval,
  product class and region length in kilobases, one row per predicted cluster.
  Three tracks read the same rows, so a run whose genome renderer is
  unavailable still has the lane view and the density profile.
find: { path_glob: "**/combgc/combgc_complete_summary.tsv" }
recipe: combgc/region_track.py
fixture: region_track.tsv
renders_as:
  # The regions on a genome axis, as intervals rather than points: `rect`
  # needs `end_col`, which is what turns each row into the cluster's real
  # footprint on the contig instead of a tick at its start.
  - id: bgc_genome_track
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: genome_view
    roles: {chr: contig, pos: start, score: length_kb, feature: region_id, end: end, category: product_class}
  # The same intervals as arrows in one lane per contig, re-parameterising the
  # pattern the ARG island track uses: several clusters packed onto one contig
  # is a biosynthetic locus, which an aggregate over product classes hides.
  - id: bgc_region_arrows
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: gene_arrow_track
    roles: {contig: contig, feature_id: region_id, start: start, end: end, strand: strand, class: product_class, label: product_class}
  # Fallback on the same collection: a plain coordinate profile that needs no
  # genome renderer, so the tab is never empty.
  - id: bgc_region_coverage
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: coverage_track
    roles: {chromosome: contig, position: start, value: length_kb, end: end, sample: sample, category: product_class}
  - { component: card, column: length_kb, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: region_id, aggregation: count, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: product_class, top_n_count: 4 }
  - { component: table, row_selection_enabled: true, row_selection_column: contig }

outputs.rawYaml:
id: cooltools_eigenvector

  the A/B compartment track. Sign marks the compartment, zero-crossings are
  compartment boundaries. The recipe phases E1 per sample, resolution and
  chromosome so it correlates positively with bin coverage (1 / balancing
  weight): the better-covered compartment is A, the same way at every

outputs.description: Each sample's fragment coverage split into the part that falls inside its own peaks and the part that does not, in base pairs and as a fraction. SEACR reports no read count, so the numerator is the summed region signal de-scaled by the spike-in factor and the denominator is the fragment-length histogram.
outputs.name: Fraction of coverage in peaks
outputs.rawYaml:
id: cutandrun_frip
name: Fraction of coverage in peaks
mode: peaks/frip
description: >-
  Each sample's fragment coverage split into the part that falls inside its own
  peaks and the part that does not, in base pairs and as a fraction. SEACR
  reports no read count, so the numerator is the summed region signal de-scaled
  by the spike-in factor and the denominator is the fragment-length histogram.
# The table is long on purpose, two rows per sample, so a donut or a stacked
# bar reads it as a composition without any client-side pivot. The sample-level
# FRiP is repeated on both rows, which leaves its quantiles unchanged.
find:
  path_glob: "**/*.frags.len.txt"
  path_glob_alt:
    - "**/*.seacr.peaks.*.bed"
recipe: cutandrun/frip.py
fixture: frip.tsv
renders_as:
  - { id: frip_composition_bar, component: figure, visu_type: bar, dict_kwargs: {x: sample, y: fraction, color: signal_class, title: Fragment coverage inside and outside peaks} }
  # The composition itself, then the spread of FRiP across samples and the
  # lowest FRiP in the run (on `frip`, one value per sample, not on `fraction`,
  # whose minimum is the smallest outside-peaks share).
  - { component: card, column: coverage_bp, aggregation: sum, secondary_layout: donut, breakdown_col: signal_class }
  - { component: card, column: frip, aggregation: average, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }

dict_kwargs.title: Fragment coverage inside and outside peaks

outputs.description: How concentrated each library's coverage is, as the quality metrics plotFingerprint writes beside its curve: the area under the observed cumulative-coverage curve, the same area for a perfectly uniform library of that depth, and the divergence between the two. Enriched targets sit far from the uniform reference, inputs and failed enrichments sit on top of it.
outputs.name: Fingerprint metrics
outputs.rawYaml:
id: deeptools_fingerprint_metrics
name: Fingerprint metrics
mode: signal/fingerprint
description: >-
  How concentrated each library's coverage is, as the quality metrics
  plotFingerprint writes beside its curve: the area under the observed
  cumulative-coverage curve, the same area for a perfectly uniform library of
  that depth, and the divergence between the two. Enriched targets sit far from
  the uniform reference, inputs and failed enrichments sit on top of it.
find:
  path_glob: "**/*.plotFingerprint.qcmetrics.txt"
recipe: deeptools/fingerprint_metrics.py
fixture: fingerprint_metrics.tsv
renders_as:
  # Enrichment against divergence from uniform: the two axes disagree only for a
  # library whose curve is odd, so a point off the trend is the one to look at.
  # MultiQC draws the fingerprint curve itself but never this table, so the
  # per-sample numbers are only readable here.
  - { id: fingerprint_scatter, component: advanced_viz, kind: scatter_xy, roles: {x: auc, y: synthetic_js_distance, label: sample} }
  - { component: figure, visu_type: bar, dict_kwargs: {x: sample, y: auc_ratio, title: Coverage concentration relative to a uniform library} }
  - { component: card, column: auc_ratio, aggregation: average, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: auc_ratio, aggregation: max, secondary_layout: threshold, threshold_value: 0.85, threshold_direction: max, threshold_warn: 0.95 }
  - { component: card, column: synthetic_js_distance, aggregation: average, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: histogram }
  - { component: card, column: x_intercept, aggregation: average, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: table }

dict_kwargs.title: Coverage concentration relative to a uniform library

outputs.description: The mean signal of every library across the plotted window, one row per bin. With `computeMatrix scale-regions` the window is the flanking region plus a gene body stretched to a fixed number of bins; with `reference-point` it is a window centred on one anchor. `bin_label` carries deepTools' own anchors, so the marker can be placed without hard-coding the window.
outputs.name: Metagene signal profile
outputs.rawYaml:

id: deseq2_vst_distribution
name: Sample expression distributions
mode: exploratory/distribution
description: >-
  Per-sample density of the variance-stabilised expression matrix, binned on a
  grid shared by every sample so the curves are directly comparable, plus each
  sample's five-number summary. The features sitting at the matrix floor are
  excluded from the grid, because the spike they form is tall enough to flatten
  the rest of the curve, and published as a share instead. This is the panel that
  says whether a library is shaped like its neighbours at all, which a PCA cannot.
find: { path_glob: "**/all.vst.tsv" }
recipe: deseq2/vst_distribution.py
fixture: vst_distribution.tsv
renders_as:
  - id: distribution_profile
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: profile
    roles: { series: sample_id, x: bin_centre, y: density }
  - {
      component: card,
      column: median,
      aggregation: range,
      aggregations: [box_plot_stats],
      secondary_layout: box_plot,
    }
  - {
      component: card,
      column: floor_share,
      aggregation: average,
      secondary_layout: gauge,
      coverage_max: 1,
    }
  - { component: card, column: sample_id, aggregation: nunique, secondary_layout: donut, breakdown_col: group }
  - { component: table }

tools.description: Differential exon / transcript usage testing, finding genes whose exon or isoform usage shifts between conditions. nf-core/nanoseq runs it on Bambu's transcript counts; nf-core/rnasplice runs it on exon bins and on transcript-level salmon counts.
tools.name: DEXSeq

outputs.description: DEXSeq differential transcript usage (DTU) as nf-core/rnasplice's dexseq_dtu route writes it: one row per contrast and transcript with its usage log2 fold change (treatment over control), p-value, adjusted p-value and the gene-level q-value.
outputs.name: Differential transcript usage

outputs.description: DEXSeq differential exon usage as nf-core/rnasplice's dexseq_exon route writes it, summarised to one row per contrast and gene: the gene-level q-value, how many exonic bins were tested and called, and the most significant bin's log2 fold change, oriented treatment over control.
outputs.name: Differential exon usage per gene

outputs.description: DEXSeq per-transcript usage statistics from nanoseq's Bambu-based differential expression subworkflow, with the significance call precomputed on the gene-level adjusted q-value.
outputs.name: Differential exon/transcript usage

tools.description: Differential exon usage with edgeR's diffSpliceDGE: an exon-level test, a gene-level F-test and a Simes-combined gene test per contrast, run by nf-core/rnasplice on featureCounts exon counts.
tools.name: edgeR diffSpliceDGE

outputs.description: edgeR diffSpliceDGE as nf-core/rnasplice's edger_exon route writes it, one row per contrast and gene: the gene-level F-test and Simes FDRs, how many exons were tested and called, and the most significant exon's relative log2 fold change (treatment over control).
outputs.name: Differential exon usage per gene (edgeR)

tools.description: Immcantation R package that drives nf-core/airrflow's adaptive immune receptor repertoire (AIRR) analysis: clonal assignment, nearest-neighbour distance threshold finding, and the clonal diversity / abundance / overlap report.
tools.name: enchantR

outputs.description: alakazam rank-abundance curve per sample: the bootstrapped relative abundance of every clone against its rank within the sample, with the confidence band the bootstrap gives it. The band is what separates a genuinely expanded head from one estimated off a handful of sequences.
outputs.name: Clonal rank abundance
outputs.rawYaml:
id: enchantr_clonal_abundance
name: Clonal rank abundance
mode: repertoire-analysis/abundance
description: >-
  alakazam rank-abundance curve per sample: the bootstrapped relative abundance
  of every clone against its rank within the sample, with the confidence band
  the bootstrap gives it. The band is what separates a genuinely expanded head
  from one estimated off a handful of sequences.
find: { path_glob: "**/repertoire_analysis_report/tables/clonal_abundance.tsv" }
recipe: enchantr/clonal_abundance.py
fixture: clonal_abundance.tsv
renders_as:
  # The curve itself: one series per sample over the rank axis, with the
  # bootstrap interval drawn as a ribbon around it.
  - id: abundance_ribbon
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: profile
    roles: { series: sample_id, x: rank, y: p, lower: lower, upper: upper }
  # How much of the repertoire the single largest clone holds, per sample.
  - {
      component: card,
      column: p,
      aggregation: max,
      aggregations: [box_plot_stats],
      secondary_layout: box_plot,
    }
  # How wide the interval is where it matters, i.e. how well backed the head is.
  - {
      component: card,
      column: upper,
      aggregation: average,
      secondary_layout: top_n,
      breakdown_col: sample_id,
      top_n_count: 3,
    }
  - { component: table }

outputs.description: alakazam Hill diversity profile per sample: the bootstrapped diversity d at every order q from richness to inverse Simpson, with its confidence band and the matching evenness.
outputs.name: Clonal diversity profile
outputs.rawYaml:
id: enchantr_clonal_diversity
name: Clonal diversity profile
mode: repertoire-analysis/diversity
description: >-
  alakazam Hill diversity profile per sample: the bootstrapped diversity d at
  every order q from richness to inverse Simpson, with its confidence band and
  the matching evenness.
find: { path_glob: "**/repertoire_analysis_report/tables/clonal_diversity.tsv" }
recipe: enchantr/clonal_diversity.py
fixture: clonal_diversity.tsv
renders_as:
  # A diversity profile is a curve per sample over an ordered x: the same shape
  # a rarefaction curve has, so the rarefaction renderer draws it directly.
  - id: diversity_profile
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: rarefaction
    roles: { sample_id: sample_id, depth: q, metric: d }
  # Narrowed to one q, the same rows are one Hill number per sample with its
  # bootstrap confidence interval.
  - id: diversity_ci_bars
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: metric_ci_bars
    roles: { label: sample_id, value: d, lower: d_lower, upper: d_upper }
  - { component: table }

outputs.description: Sample by sample matrix of how many clones two samples share. Clones are defined within a subject, so samples of different subjects always read zero; the diagonal is zeroed so the colour scale spans the real sharing.
outputs.name: Clonal overlap matrix
outputs.rawYaml:
id: enchantr_clonal_overlap
name: Clonal overlap matrix
mode: repertoire-analysis/overlap
description: >-
  Sample by sample matrix of how many clones two samples share. Clones are
  defined within a subject, so samples of different subjects always read zero;
  the diagonal is zeroed so the colour scale spans the real sharing.
find: { path_glob: "**/repertoire_analysis_report/tables/clonal_overlap.tsv" }
recipe: enchantr/clonal_overlap.py
fixture: clonal_overlap.tsv
renders_as:
  - id: overlap_heatmap
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: complex_heatmap
    roles: { index: sample_id }
  # The same square matrix read as an ordination. Every sample is a row of
  # shared-clone counts, so a distance over those rows places samples that share
  # clones next to each other: the repertoire-overlap MDS immunarch and VDJtools
  # draw. The coordinates are computed at render time (the tile sets
  # `compute_method: pcoa`), never stored, so the ordination follows whatever
  # sample filter is active.
  - id: overlap_mds
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: embedding
    roles: { sample_id: sample_id, cluster: subject_id }
  - { component: table }

outputs.description: Clone by sample presence matrix. Each row is one clone of one subject and each sample column is a 0/1 membership flag, so an UpSet reads the intersections as clones shared by exactly those samples.
outputs.name: Shared clone sets
outputs.rawYaml:
id: enchantr_clone_sets
name: Shared clone sets
mode: repertoire-analysis/clone-sets
description: >-

renders_as:

  - { component: card, column: n_samples, aggregation: max, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: table }

outputs.description: Every clone of every sample with its sequence count and frequency, its rank within the sample (a rank-abundance curve) and its clonal-homeostasis size class.
outputs.name: Clone sizes
outputs.rawYaml:
id: enchantr_clone_sizes
name: Clone sizes
mode: repertoire-analysis/clone-sizes
description: >-
  Every clone of every sample with its sequence count and frequency, its rank

outputs.description: alakazam Hill diversity per sample at q = 0 (richness), q = 1 (Shannon) and q = 2 (inverse Simpson), with the bootstrap confidence interval, one labelled row per sample and order.
outputs.name: Hill diversity at the named orders
outputs.rawYaml:
id: enchantr_diversity_orders
name: Hill diversity at the named orders
mode: repertoire-analysis/diversity-orders
description: >-
  alakazam Hill diversity per sample at q = 0 (richness), q = 1 (Shannon) and
  q = 2 (inverse Simpson), with the bootstrap confidence interval, one labelled
  row per sample and order.
find: { path_glob: "**/repertoire_analysis_report/tables/clonal_diversity.tsv" }
recipe: enchantr/diversity_orders.py
fixture: diversity_orders.tsv
renders_as:
  # One order at a time (a single-choice filter on `order`) reads as one Hill
  # number per sample with its confidence whiskers.

    component: advanced_viz
    kind: metric_ci_bars

outputs.description: One row per sample: sequences that entered clonal assignment, the clones they collapsed into, the clone-size spread, and the rarefied Hill numbers with their confidence bounds.
outputs.name: Repertoire summary
outputs.rawYaml:
id: enchantr_repertoire_summary
name: Repertoire summary
mode: repertoire-analysis/summary
description: >-
  One row per sample: sequences that entered clonal assignment, the clones they
  collapsed into, the clone-size spread, and the rarefied Hill numbers with
  their confidence bounds.
find: { path_glob: "**/repertoire_analysis_report/tables/num_clones_table.tsv" }
recipe: enchantr/repertoire_summary.py
fixture: repertoire_summary.tsv
renders_as:
  - { component: card, column: number_of_clones, aggregation: sum, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: sequences_per_clone, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: shannon, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: evenness, aggregation: median, secondary_layout: threshold, threshold_value: 0.9, threshold_direction: min, threshold_warn: 0.85 }
  - component: figure
    visu_type: scatter
    dict_kwargs: { x: sequences, y: number_of_clones, color: subject_id, size: sequences_per_clone, log_x: "True", log_y: "True" }
  # Richness against evenness: the two halves of a Hill profile on one plane, so
  # a repertoire that is large but carried by a few clones separates from one
  # that is both large and flat. Size is the sequencing depth behind the point,
  # which is what a difference in richness has to be read against.
  - id: richness_evenness
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: scatter_xy
    roles: { x: richness, y: evenness, label: sample_id, color: subject_id, size: sequences }
  - { component: table, row_selection_enabled: true, row_selection_column: sample_id }

outputs.description: Sequences left after every pRESTO and Change-O step, one row per sample, with the fraction of raw reads that reach the final annotated repertoire.

outputs.description: One row per sample with the headline count of every nf-core/funcscan screen that produced a result: resistance-gene hits and distinct genes, antimicrobial peptide candidates and how many reach high confidence, biosynthetic gene cluster regions and product classes, CAZyme genes and families. The four screens share no table of their own, so this is the collection every sample filter and every cross-screen comparison hangs off.
outputs.name: Screening hub
outputs.rawYaml:
id: funcscan_screening_summary
name: Screening hub
mode: screening/summary
description: >-
  One row per sample with the headline count of every nf-core/funcscan screen
  that produced a result: resistance-gene hits and distinct genes, antimicrobial
  peptide candidates and how many reach high confidence, biosynthetic gene
  cluster regions and product classes, CAZyme genes and families. The four
  screens share no table of their own, so this is the collection every sample
  filter and every cross-screen comparison hangs off.
# The hub is derived from whichever screens ran, so any one of the four
# aggregated reports is enough to recognise the run.
find:
  path_glob: "**/hamronization_summarize/*combined_report.tsv"
  path_glob_alt:
    - "**/hamronization/*combined_report.tsv"
    - "**/ampcombi2/Ampcombi_summary.tsv"
    - "**/combgc/combgc_complete_summary.tsv"
    - "**/cazyme_annotation/*/*_overview.tsv"
recipe: funcscan/screening_summary.py
fixture: screening_summary.tsv
renders_as:
  # Resistome load against carbohydrate-degradation capacity: the two screens
  # that scale with assembly size, so a sample far off the cloud is either
  # unusually resistant or unusually poorly assembled. Size is the BGC count
  # and the lasso emits the sample the rest of the dashboard filters on. The
  # colour channel is left to the tile: every string column here is the sample
  # itself, so a colour role would only repeat the label, while a numeric
  # `color_col` on the tile carries the third screen.
  - id: screen_scatter
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: scatter_xy
    roles: {x: arg_hits, y: cazymes, label: sample, size: bgc_regions}
  # The four screens differ by two orders of magnitude, so the bars need a log
  # axis; a sample missing a colour returned nothing for that screen.
  - id: screen_composition
    component: figure
    code: |
      # The colour channel belongs to the screen here, so the dashboard's
      # analysis groups take the facet axis instead: one band of samples per
      # group. Spread into the reshape below too, or the unpivot would drop the
      # annotation column before the facet could read it.
      index_cols = ["sample"] + [c for c in depictio_group_by if c != "sample"]
      grp_col = depictio_group_by[0] if depictio_group_by else None

      # wide -> long so each screen becomes its own bar colour
      df_modified = df.unpivot(
          index=index_cols,
          on=["arg_hits", "amp_candidates", "bgc_regions", "cazymes"],
          variable_name="screen",
          value_name="findings",
      ).filter(pl.col("findings") > 0)

      labels = {
          "arg_hits": "ARG hits",
          "amp_candidates": "AMP candidates",
          "bgc_regions": "BGC regions",
          "cazymes": "CAZymes",
      }
      df_modified = df_modified.with_columns(
          pl.col("screen").replace_strict(labels, default=pl.col("screen")).alias("screen")
      )

      fig = px.bar(
          df_modified.to_pandas(),
          x="sample",
          y="findings",
          color="screen",
          barmode="group",
          log_y=True,
          facet_col=grp_col,
          category_orders={"screen": list(labels.values())},
      )
      fig.update_layout(
          yaxis_title="Findings (log scale)",
          legend_title_text="Screen",
          margin={"t": 24, "l": 56, "r": 16, "b": 80},
      )
      if grp_col:
          # Each panel keeps only its own samples, and its title is the group
          # name rather than the annotation column's name and an equals sign.
          fig.update_xaxes(matches=None, showticklabels=True, title_text="")
          fig.for_each_annotation(lambda a: a.update(text=a.text.split("=")[-1]))
      else:
          fig.update_layout(xaxis_title="Sample")
  - { component: card, column: arg_hits, aggregation: sum, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: sample, top_n_count: 4 }
  - { component: card, column: arg_genes, aggregation: sum, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: sample, top_n_count: 4 }
  - { component: card, column: amp_candidates, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: amp_high_confidence, aggregation: sum, secondary_layout: composition, breakdown_col: sample, top_n_count: 4 }
  - { component: card, column: bgc_regions, aggregation: sum, secondary_layout: donut, breakdown_col: sample, top_n_count: 4 }
  - { component: card, column: bgc_classes, aggregation: max, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: sample, top_n_count: 4 }
  - { component: card, column: cazymes, aggregation: average, secondary_layout: gauge, coverage_max: 1500.0 }
  - { component: card, column: cazyme_families, aggregation: average, secondary_layout: histogram }
  - { component: table, row_selection_enabled: true, row_selection_column: sample }

index_cols = ["sample"] + [c for c in depictio_group_by if c != "sample"]

outputs.name: Validated fusions
outputs.rawYaml:
id: fusioninspector_fusions
name: Validated fusions
mode: fusions/abridged
description: >-
  One row per fusion transcript pair that survived FusionInspector's
  re-alignment, with the junction and spanning read support, the normalised
  expression (FFPM), the fusion-allele ratios against each partner, and the
  protein-level consequence of the fusion.
find: { path_glob: "**/fusioninspector/*/*.FusionInspector.fusions.abridged.tsv" }
recipe: fusioninspector/fusions.py
fixture: fusions.tsv
renders_as:
  # Expression against junction purity, one dot per fusion, grouped by the
  # protein consequence: an in-frame fusion carried by mostly junction reads
  # sits top-right, a frameshift held up by spanning fragments bottom-left.
  - { id: evidence_dot_plot, component: advanced_viz, kind: dot_plot, roles: {cluster: prot_fusion_type, gene: fusion, mean_expression: log_ffpm, frac_expressing: junction_fraction} }
  # The two fusion-allele ratios against each other. A fusion dominant on both
  # partners lands top-right; a ratio near the axis means the wild-type allele
  # of that partner still dominates.
  - component: figure
    code: |
      # FAR can be reported as 0, which a log axis cannot place, so shift both.
      eps = 0.01
      df_modified = df.with_columns(
          (pl.col("far_left") + eps).alias("far_left_shift"),
          (pl.col("far_right") + eps).alias("far_right_shift"),
      )

      fig = px.scatter(
          df_modified.to_pandas(),
          x="far_left_shift", y="far_right_shift",
          color="prot_fusion_type", size="supporting_reads",
          size_max=24, opacity=0.8, log_x=True, log_y=True,
          hover_name="fusion",
      )
      fig.update_layout(
          xaxis_title="FAR 5' partner (log)",
          yaxis_title="FAR 3' partner (log)",
          legend_title_text="Protein fusion type",
          margin={"t": 24, "l": 56, "r": 16, "b": 48},
      )
  - { component: card, column: ffpm, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: fusion, aggregation: nunique, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: prot_fusion_type, top_n_count: 3 }
  - { component: card, column: supporting_reads, aggregation: sum, secondary_layout: donut, breakdown_col: splice_type }
  - { component: card, column: junction_fraction, aggregation: average, secondary_layout: histogram }
  - { component: table, row_selection_enabled: true, row_selection_column: fusion }

renders_as.code:
# FAR can be reported as 0, which a log axis cannot place, so shift both.
eps = 0.01
df_modified = df.with_columns(
    (pl.col("far_left") + eps).alias("far_left_shift"),
    (pl.col("far_right") + eps).alias("far_right_shift"),
)

fig = px.scatter(
    df_modified.to_pandas(),
    x="far_left_shift", y="far_right_shift",
    color="prot_fusion_type", size="supporting_reads",
    size_max=24, opacity=0.8, log_x=True, log_y=True,
    hover_name="fusion",
)
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="FAR 5' partner (log)",
    yaxis_title="FAR 3' partner (log)",
    legend_title_text="Protein fusion type",
    margin={"t": 24, "l": 56, "r": 16, "b": 48},
)

outputs.name: Fusion protein domains
outputs.rawYaml:
id: fusioninspector_protein_domains
name: Fusion protein domains
mode: fusions/pfam
description: >-
  The Pfam domains FusionInspector annotates on the 5' and 3' partner of each
  fusion protein, unpivoted from the packed PFAM_LEFT / PFAM_RIGHT fields into
  one row per domain with its amino-acid span and e-value.
find: { path_glob: "**/fusioninspector/*/*.FusionInspector.fusions.abridged.tsv" }
recipe: fusioninspector/protein_domains.py
fixture: protein_domains.tsv
renders_as:
  # The fusion protein drawn as its two partners end to end, each annotated
  # domain placed along the partner that contributes it and the breakpoint
  # marked between them. A domain the breakpoint truncated is short where the
  # same domain kept whole on the other side is not.
  - { id: fusion_domains, component: advanced_viz, kind: fusion_structure, roles: {fusion_id: fusion, partner: partner, feature: domain, start: domain_start, end: domain_end} }
  # Domain starts along the fusion protein, one lane per fusion, split by the
  # partner that contributes the domain. Kept beside the structure view: it
  # ranks many fusions at a glance where the structure reads a handful closely.
  - { id: domain_lollipop, component: advanced_viz, kind: lollipop, roles: {feature_id: fusion, position: domain_start, category: partner} }
  # Domain extents as bars, so a domain the breakpoint truncated is visibly
  # shorter than the same domain kept whole on the other side.
  - { component: figure, visu_type: bar, dict_kwargs: {x: domain, y: domain_length, color: partner} }
  - { component: card, column: domain, aggregation: nunique, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: partner, top_n_count: 3 }
  - { component: card, column: domain_length, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: neg_log10_evalue, aggregation: average, secondary_layout: histogram }
  - { component: table, row_selection_enabled: true, row_selection_column: fusion }

outputs.name: GSEA enrichment report
outputs.rawYaml:
id: gsea_report
name: GSEA enrichment report
mode: enrichment/gsea
description: >-
  Gene sets enriched at one pole of a contrast, from the report tables a
  pre-ranked GSEA run publishes. Neither the contrast nor the pole is a column of
  those files, so the recipe recovers both from the file name and stacks every
  report into one frame. The leading-edge percentage is parsed out of the string
  GSEA writes for a human reader, and an FDR q-value of zero, which is what GSEA
  writes below its resolution, is clipped at the run's own floor rather than sent
  to infinity.
find:
  path_glob: "**/tables/gsea/**/*.gsea_report_for_*.tsv"
recipe: gsea/report.py
fixture: report.tsv
renders_as:
  # The signature panel: one dot per set, placed on its normalised enrichment
  # score, sized by how many of its genes were found and coloured by
  # significance, split by the pole the set came up at.
  - id: gsea_dotplot
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: enrichment
    roles:
      { term: term, nes: nes, padj: fdr_qvalue, gene_count: size, source: phenotype }
  # The same scores as ranked bars, which is the view that compares two
  # contrasts rather than two poles of one.
  - id: gsea_nes_bars
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: da_barplot
    roles:
      { feature_id: term, contrast: contrast, lfc: nes, significance: fdr_qvalue, label: phenotype }
  - {
      component: card,
      column: term,
      aggregation: nunique,
      secondary_layout: top_n,
      breakdown_col: phenotype,
      top_n_count: 4,
    }
  # On |NES|: the strongest set can sit at the negative pole.
  - {
      component: card,
      column: abs_nes,
      aggregation: max,
      aggregations: [box_plot_stats],
      secondary_layout: box_plot,
    }
  - {
      component: card,
      column: fdr_qvalue,
      aggregation: median,
      secondary_layout: threshold,
      threshold_value: 0.05,
      threshold_direction: max,
      threshold_warn: 0.25,
    }
  - {
      component: card,
      column: leading_edge_percent,
      aggregation: median,
      aggregations: [box_plot_stats],
      secondary_layout: box_plot,
    }
  - { component: table, row_selection_enabled: true, row_selection_column: term }

outputs.name: Bin taxonomy
outputs.rawYaml:
id: gtdbtk_summary
name: Bin taxonomy
mode: summary
description: >-
  Which organism each recovered bin is, placed against the Genome Taxonomy
  Database. The lineage is split into one column per rank, so a phylum becomes
  a filter that reaches every other tile and the deepest rank a bin reached
  becomes a readable number instead of a string to squint at.
find:
  path_glob: "**/classify/*.summary.tsv"
  path_glob_alt:
    - "**/gtdbtk*.bac*.summary.tsv"
    - "**/gtdbtk*.ar*.summary.tsv"
    - "**/*.bac*.summary.tsv"
    - "**/*.ar*.summary.tsv"
recipe: gtdbtk/summary.py
fixture: summary.tsv
renders_as:
  - { id: lineage_sunburst, component: advanced_viz, kind: sunburst,
      roles: {ranks: [domain, phylum, class_name, order, family, genus], abundance: bin_count} }
  - { id: assembler_binner_phylum, component: advanced_viz, kind: sankey,
      roles: {steps: [assembler, binner, phylum]} }
  - { id: ani_vs_alignment, component: advanced_viz, kind: scatter_xy,
      roles: {x: closest_ani, y: closest_af, label: bin_id, color: phylum} }
  - { component: figure, visu_type: bar, dict_kwargs: {x: phylum, y: bin_count, color: binner, title: Bins recovered per phylum} }
  - { component: card, column: bin_id, aggregation: nunique,
      secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: phylum, top_n_count: 5 }
  - { component: card, column: species, aggregation: nunique,
      secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: genus, top_n_count: 5 }
  - { component: card, column: bin_id, aggregation: nunique,
      secondary_layout: donut, breakdown_col: rank_assigned }
  - { component: card, column: closest_ani, aggregation: median,
      aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  # closest_af and not msa_percent: GTDB-Tk fills msa_percent only on the
  # pplacer path, and a run classified through ANI screening leaves it empty
  # for every bin, which makes a card over it a column of blanks.
  - { component: card, column: closest_af, aggregation: average,
      aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: histogram }
  - { component: table }

outputs.name: Transcript structures
outputs.rawYaml:
id: gtf_transcripts
name: Transcript structures
mode: exon-blocks
description: >-
  Exon and CDS blocks of every transcript in a run's GTF/GFF annotations, one
  row per block, carrying the gene, the strand, the novelty class and the
  per-transcript expression when the writer recorded one.
find:
  path_glob: "**/*.gtf"
  path_glob_alt: # compressed annotations, and bambu's run-level extended one
    - "**/*.gtf.gz"
    - "**/bambu/extended_annotations.gtf"
recipe: gtf/transcripts.py
fixture: transcripts.tsv
renders_as:
  - id: transcript_structures
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: transcript_structure
    roles:
      transcript_id: transcript_id
      gene_id: gene_id
      chrom: chrom
      start: start
      end: end
      feature: feature
      strand: strand
      sample: sample
      gene_name: gene_name
      transcript_class: transcript_class
      expression: expression
  # How many isoforms the annotation carries, and which genes carry most of
  # them: the one number that says whether a run found novel structure at all.
  - { component: card, column: transcript_id, aggregation: nunique, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: gene_name, top_n_count: 3 }
  # Expression is long-tailed across isoforms, so the Tukey strip says more
  # about it than the median on its own.
  - { component: card, column: expression, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: table }

outputs.name: ARG hits
outputs.rawYaml:
id: hamronization_report
name: ARG hits
mode: arg/hits
description: >-
  One row per antimicrobial-resistance gene hit, with the sample recovered from
  the per-tool input file name and the drug class, screening tool, reference
  database, identity and coverage normalised across every ARG tool.
find:
  path_glob: "**/hamronization_summarize/*combined_report.tsv"
  path_glob_alt: ["**/hamronization/*combined_report.tsv"]
recipe: hamronization/report.py
fixture: report.tsv
renders_as:
  # The resistance genes as strand-aware arrows along their contig, one lane
  # per contig. Where several ARGs sit head to tail on one contig, that is a
  # resistance island, and no aggregate over drug classes can show it.
  # Coloured by tool, not by drug class: the report holds one row per (tool,
  # hit), so a single locus called by four screens draws four stacked arrows,
  # and the tool is what tells them apart. drug_class would be the biological
  # axis but hAMRonization does not normalise it, so AMINOGLYCOSIDE,
  # aminoglycoside and "aminoglycoside antibiotic" would each take a hue of
  # their own and the island would read as more diverse than it is.
  - { id: arg_island_track, component: advanced_viz, kind: gene_arrow_track, roles: {contig: contig, feature_id: gene_symbol, start: start, end: stop, strand: strand, class: tool} }
  # Screen -> drug class -> gene: which tool contributes which part of the
  # resistome. hAMRonization does not normalise the drug-class vocabulary
  # across tools, so the tool ring keeps the three vocabularies apart.
  - { id: arg_hierarchy, component: advanced_viz, kind: sunburst, roles: {ranks: [tool, drug_class, gene_symbol], abundance: hits} }
  - { component: card, column: hits, aggregation: sum, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: drug_class, top_n_count: 4 }
  - { component: card, column: gene_symbol, aggregation: nunique, secondary_layout: donut, breakdown_col: tool }
  - { component: card, column: identity_pct, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: coverage_pct, aggregation: average, secondary_layout: threshold, threshold_value: 80.0, threshold_direction: min, threshold_warn: 90.0 }
  - { component: table, row_selection_enabled: true, row_selection_column: gene_symbol }

id: hicpro_pair_flow
name: Read-pair fates
mode: stats
description: >-
  The same HiC-Pro statistics as one weighted row per read-pair fate, mapping
  to restriction-fragment filter to contact class, so the funnel can be drawn
  as a flow and the cis/trans split as a composition.
find:
  path_glob: "**/*_allValidPairs.mergestat"
  path_glob_alt:

    - "**/*.mRSstat"
recipe: hicpro/pair_flow.py
fixture: pair_flow.tsv
renders_as:
  - id: pair_flow_sankey
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: sankey
    roles:
      steps: [mapping, filtering, contacts]
  # Composition of what survives: the cis/trans split plus the duplicates
  # de-duplication removed. `filter_expr` keeps the lost paths out of the ring.
  - component: card
    column: pairs
    aggregation: sum
    secondary_layout: donut
    breakdown_col: contacts
    filter_expr: "col('filtering') == 'Valid pairs'"
  - component: card
    column: pairs
    aggregation: sum
    secondary_layout: donut
    breakdown_col: mapping
  - { component: table }

outputs.description: How each sample's peaks are distributed around the nearest transcription start site, counted in 250 bp bins across a 20 kb window. A sharp central spike means the peaks are promoter-bound; a flat curve means they sit across gene bodies and intergenic space.
outputs.name: Distance to nearest TSS
outputs.rawYaml:
id: homer_tss_distance_profile
name: Distance to nearest TSS
mode: peaks/tss_distance
description: >-
  How each sample's peaks are distributed around the nearest transcription start
  site, counted in 250 bp bins across a 20 kb window. A sharp central spike
  means the peaks are promoter-bound; a flat curve means they sit across gene
  bodies and intergenic space.
find:
  path_glob: "**/*_peaks.annotatePeaks.txt"
recipe: homer/tss_distance_profile.py
fixture: tss_distance_profile.tsv
renders_as:
  # The `profile` kind rather than a histogram figure: it owns the marker at the
  # start site, the shaded promoter window and the log axis in the tile's own
  # Settings, which is what the code-mode TSS histograms were written to get.
  - { id: tss_distance, component: advanced_viz, kind: profile, roles: {series: sample, x: distance_to_tss, y: fraction} }
  - { component: figure, visu_type: line, dict_kwargs: {x: distance_to_tss, y: fraction, color: sample, title: Peak distribution around the nearest TSS} }
  - { component: card, column: peak_count, aggregation: sum, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: sample, top_n_count: 3 }
  - { component: card, column: fraction, aggregation: max, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: peak_count, aggregation: sum, secondary_layout: composition, breakdown_col: sample }
  - { component: table }

dict_kwargs.title: Peak distribution around the nearest TSS

  Sample by gene mutation matrix derived from the long variant table, one row

  - { id: mutation_matrix, component: advanced_viz, kind: oncoplot, roles: {sample_id: sample_id, gene: gene, mutation_type: mutation_type} }

  # cannot fall back to an empty bar on a run that omits an optional column.
  - { component: card, column: sample_id, aggregation: nunique, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: gene, top_n_count: 3 }

  - { component: table }

  # nf-core dashboards were already computing off this output by hand.
  - { component: card, column: gene, aggregation: nunique, secondary_layout: composition, breakdown_col: mutation_type }

tools.description: K-mer counting and the read k-mer spectrum.
tools.name: Jellyfish

outputs.description: The k-mer multiplicity histogram of each read set, cut past the main peak. The main peak sits at the k-mer depth of the sequencing; a second peak at half that depth is the heterozygous share of the genome, and a long right tail the repeats. It is the curve GenomeScope fits, so a genome size estimate can be checked against it by eye.
outputs.name: Read k-mer spectrum
outputs.rawYaml:
id: jellyfish_histogram
name: Read k-mer spectrum
mode: histo
description: >-
  The k-mer multiplicity histogram of each read set, cut past the main peak.
  The main peak sits at the k-mer depth of the sequencing; a second peak at half
  that depth is the heterozygous share of the genome, and a long right tail the
  repeats. It is the curve GenomeScope fits, so a genome size estimate can be
  checked against it by eye.
find:
  path_glob: "**/jellyfish/histo/*.tsv"
  path_glob_alt:
    - "**/*.histo"
recipe: jellyfish/histogram.py
fixture: histogram.tsv
renders_as:
  - { id: kmer_spectrum, component: advanced_viz, kind: profile,
      roles: {series: read_set, x: multiplicity, y: kmers} }
  - { id: kmer_mass_spectrum, component: advanced_viz, kind: profile,
      roles: {series: read_set, x: multiplicity, y: kmer_mass} }
  - { component: figure, visu_type: line, dict_kwargs: {x: multiplicity, y: kmers, color: read_set, title: Read k-mer spectrum} }
  - { component: card, column: peak_multiplicity, aggregation: median,
      aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: table }

outputs.description: Reads processed and pseudoaligned by kallisto bus, barcodes on the 10x whitelist after correction, and the cells kb count --filter called, one row per sample.
outputs.fixtureContent:
sample	n_processed	n_pseudoaligned	p_pseudoaligned	n_barcodes	cells_called
pbmc8k	784064148	467812652	0.597	1311043	8514
outputs.name: Run headline numbers (kallisto | bustools)
outputs.rawYaml:
id: kallisto_run_metrics
name: Run headline numbers (kallisto | bustools)
mode: kallisto/run_metrics
description: >-
  Reads processed and pseudoaligned by kallisto bus, barcodes on the 10x
  whitelist after correction, and the cells kb count --filter called, one
  row per sample.
find:
  path_glob: "**/*.count/run_info.json"
recipe: kallisto/run_metrics.py
fixture: run_metrics.tsv
renders_as:
  - { component: card, column: p_pseudoaligned, aggregation: average, secondary_layout: gauge, coverage_max: 1.0 }
  - { component: card, column: cells_called, aggregation: max, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: n_barcodes, aggregation: max, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: table }

outputs.description: Every MACS2 broad peak of every sample in one table, with the region width, its centre and the fold enrichment, p-value and q-value MACS2 reported for it. A broad call has no summit, so the region centre stands in for it.
outputs.name: Broad peak calls
outputs.rawYaml:
id: macs2_broad_peaks
name: Broad peak calls
mode: peaks/broad
description: >-
  Every MACS2 broad peak of every sample in one table, with the region width,
  its centre and the fold enrichment, p-value and q-value MACS2 reported for
  it. A broad call has no summit, so the region centre stands in for it.
# The narrow twin is `macs2_peaks` (*_peaks.narrowPeak, BED6+4 with a summit
# column). A run calls one or the other, so the two globs never both match.
find:
  path_glob: "**/*_peaks.broadPeak"
recipe: macs2/broad_peaks.py
fixture: broad_peaks.tsv
renders_as:
  # Significance along the genome, then how wide the regions are.
  - { id: broad_peak_significance, component: advanced_viz, kind: manhattan, roles: {chr: chr, pos: midpoint, score: neg_log10_qvalue} }
  - { component: figure, visu_type: histogram, dict_kwargs: {x: width, color: sample, title: Peak width distribution} }
  # How many regions and where they concentrate, then the spread of width,
  # enrichment and significance behind that count.
  - { component: card, column: peak_id, aggregation: count, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: sample, top_n_count: 3 }
  - { component: card, column: width, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: fold_enrichment, aggregation: average, secondary_layout: histogram }
  - { component: card, column: neg_log10_qvalue, aggregation: max, secondary_layout: threshold, threshold_value: 1.3, threshold_direction: min, threshold_warn: 1.0 }
  - { component: table, row_selection_enabled: true, row_selection_column: peak_id }

  - { component: card, column: support, aggregation: count, secondary_layout: donut, breakdown_col: support }

outputs.description: One row per sample: how many peaks MACS2 called, the FRiP score, and the median, mean and maximum of peak width, fold enrichment and significance across those peaks.
outputs.name: Peak QC summary
outputs.rawYaml:
id: macs2_peak_summary
name: Peak QC summary
mode: peaks/qc
description: >-
  One row per sample: how many peaks MACS2 called, the FRiP score, and the
  median, mean and maximum of peak width, fold enrichment and significance
  across those peaks.
# The long summary table the peak-QC step writes next to the calls; the FRiP
# score is joined on from the sibling MultiQC custom-content files.
find:
  path_glob: "**/*peak.summary.txt"
recipe: macs2/peak_summary.py
fixture: peak_summary.tsv
renders_as:
  # Signal-to-noise per sample, then the yield behind it.
  - { component: figure, visu_type: bar, dict_kwargs: {x: sample, y: frip_score, color: sample, title: FRiP score per sample} }
  - { component: card, column: num_peaks, aggregation: sum, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: sample, top_n_count: 3 }
  - { component: card, column: frip_score, aggregation: average, secondary_layout: gauge, coverage_max: 1.0 }
  - { component: card, column: width_median, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: fold_enrichment_median, aggregation: average, secondary_layout: threshold, threshold_value: 5.0 }
  - { component: table }

outputs.description: Every MACS2 narrow peak of every sample in one table, with the summit position, the peak width and the fold enrichment, p-value and q-value MACS2 reported for it.
outputs.name: Peak calls
outputs.rawYaml:
id: macs2_peaks
name: Peak calls
mode: peaks/narrow
description: >-
  Every MACS2 narrow peak of every sample in one table, with the summit
  position, the peak width and the fold enrichment, p-value and q-value MACS2
  reported for it.
# `--broad` writes *_peaks.broadPeak, a BED6+3 with no summit column: a
# different schema, so it is not folded in here as an alternate glob.
find:
  path_glob: "**/*_peaks.narrowPeak"
recipe: macs2/peaks.py
fixture: peaks.tsv
renders_as:
  # Significance along the genome, then how wide the calls are.
  - { id: peak_significance, component: advanced_viz, kind: manhattan, roles: {chr: chr, pos: summit, score: neg_log10_qvalue} }
  # The same rows on a chromosome-aware locus axis, drawn by GenomeSpy. A peak is
  # an interval and not a point, so `end` is bound and a dashboard draws it with
  # `mark: rect`; the Manhattan above keeps the summit-as-a-point reading.
  # `sample` is bound so a tile can stack one lane per library without rebinding.
  - { id: peak_genome_view, component: advanced_viz, kind: genome_view, roles: {chr: chr, pos: start, score: neg_log10_qvalue, feature: peak_id, end: end, sample: sample} }
  # The same intervals in plain Plotly, so a section that leads with the GenomeSpy
  # track still says something if that renderer is unavailable. Enrichment rather
  # than significance on the y axis: it is the quantity a coverage-shaped reading
  # of a peak set is about.
  - { id: peak_coverage_track, component: advanced_viz, kind: coverage_track, roles: {chromosome: chr, position: start, value: fold_enrichment, end: end, sample: sample} }
  # Enrichment against significance. MACS2 reports significance already as
  # -log10, so a tile binding this sets `significance_is_neg_log10: true`.
  - { id: peak_volcano, component: advanced_viz, kind: volcano, roles: {feature_id: peak_id, effect_size: fold_enrichment, significance: neg_log10_qvalue, label: peak_id, category: sample} }
  - { component: figure, visu_type: histogram, dict_kwargs: {x: width, color: sample, title: Peak width distribution} }
  # How many peaks and where they concentrate, then the spread of width,
  # enrichment and significance behind that count.
  - { component: card, column: peak_id, aggregation: count, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: sample, top_n_count: 3 }
  - { component: card, column: width, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: fold_enrichment, aggregation: average, secondary_layout: histogram }
  - { component: card, column: neg_log10_qvalue, aggregation: max, secondary_layout: threshold, threshold_value: 1.3, threshold_direction: min, threshold_warn: 1.0 }
  - { component: table, row_selection_enabled: true, row_selection_column: peak_id }

outputs.description: The peak calls of every sample aggregated on a 4 kb window centred on their summits, in 50 bp bins: the share of the sample's peaks still covering each offset (the average peak footprint), and how densely the other samples of the run place their own summits around this sample's summits. Derived from the narrowPeak intervals only, so it is a peak-call aggregate and not a read coverage metagene.

  offset (the average peak footprint), and how densely the other samples of the

outputs.description: One row per assembly: the consensus quality value Merqury derives from k-mers found in the assembly but not in the reads, and the share of solid read k-mers the assembly recovers. When mosdepth runs against a target file it reports every contig twice, once genome-wide and once over the targets only; the recipe splits that into a `scope` column (genome or region) instead of mixing two very different depths on one axis. Sample and alignment stage come from the file name, one pass is kept per sample, and only the primary contigs and the run total are kept, which drops the thousands of ALT, decoy and HLA rows a GRCh38 run lists.

  bases of sequence that landed on it and the mean, minimum and maximum
  depth. When mosdepth runs against a target file it reports every contig
  twice, once genome-wide and once over the targets only; the recipe splits
  that into a `scope` column (genome or region) instead of mixing two very
  different depths on one axis. Sample and alignment stage come from the file
  name, one pass is kept per sample, and only the primary contigs and the run
  total are kept, which drops the thousands of ALT, decoy and HLA rows a

  - { component: card, column: mean_depth, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: table }

outputs.description: Mean depth on chromosome X and on chromosome Y for every library, from the small per-run table MultiQC's mosdepth module writes, split per sample and alignment stage. The X/Y depth ratio separates the two common karyotypes cleanly: two X and no Y leaves almost no Y signal and a large ratio, one X and one Y sits near 1. `inferred_sex` applies a 10x cut-off in the empty band between them. It is a heuristic on two summary numbers, not a genotype call, and a sex chromosome aneuploidy, a mixed or contaminated library or a very low-depth run can all land on the wrong side of it. Read it as a check against the sex recorded in the sample sheet, and read the raw X and Y depths beside it to see how far from the cut-off a library actually sits.
outputs.name: X and Y coverage sex check

  Mean depth on chromosome X and on chromosome Y for every library, from the
  small per-run table MultiQC's mosdepth module writes, split per sample and
  alignment stage. The X/Y depth ratio separates the two common karyotypes
  cleanly: two X and no Y leaves almost no Y signal and a large ratio, one X
  and one Y sits near 1. `inferred_sex` applies a 10x cut-off in the empty
  band between them. It is a heuristic on two summary numbers, not a genotype
  call, and a sex chromosome aneuploidy, a mixed or contaminated library or a
  very low-depth run can all land on the wrong side of it. Read it as a check
  against the sex recorded in the sample sheet, and read the raw X and Y
  depths beside it to see how far from the cut-off a library actually sits.

outputs.description: How many distinct molecules each library would yield at a given sequencing depth, with the 95% interval preseq puts around that extrapolation. A curve still climbing at the depth already sequenced means resequencing buys new material; one that has flattened means the library is exhausted.
outputs.name: Library complexity curve
outputs.rawYaml:
id: preseq_complexity_curve
name: Library complexity curve
mode: complexity-curve
description: >-
  How many distinct molecules each library would yield at a given sequencing
  depth, with the 95% interval preseq puts around that extrapolation. A curve
  still climbing at the depth already sequenced means resequencing buys new
  material; one that has flattened means the library is exhausted.
find:
  path_glob: "**/*.ccurve.txt"
recipe: preseq/complexity_curve.py
fixture: complexity_curve.tsv
renders_as:
  # The curve with its interval as a ribbon. This is the whole reason the tool
  # has an entry of its own: MultiQC's preseq panel plots expected_distinct
  # alone and drops the two CI columns, so the width of the extrapolation is
  # only readable here.
  - { id: complexity_ribbon, component: advanced_viz, kind: profile, roles: {series: sample, x: total_reads, y: expected_distinct, lower: lower_ci, upper: upper_ci} }
  - { component: figure, visu_type: line, dict_kwargs: {x: total_reads, y: expected_distinct, color: sample, title: Expected distinct molecules by sequencing depth} }
  - { component: card, column: expected_distinct, aggregation: max, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: sample, top_n_count: 3 }
  - { component: card, column: expected_distinct, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: ci_width, aggregation: average, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: histogram }
  - { component: card, column: expected_distinct, aggregation: sum, secondary_layout: composition, breakdown_col: sample }
  - { component: table }

dict_kwargs.title: Expected distinct molecules by sequencing depth

outputs.description: Multi-metric alpha-diversity per sample (shannon, evenness, faith_pd…).
outputs.name: Alpha diversity
outputs.rawYaml:
id: qiime2_alpha_diversity
name: Alpha diversity
mode: diversity
description: Multi-metric alpha-diversity per sample (shannon, evenness, faith_pd…).
nf_core_url: https://github.com/nf-core/modules/tree/master/modules/nf-core/qiime2/diversitycore
find: { path_glob: "**/qiime2/diversity/alpha_diversity/*_vector/metadata.tsv" }
recipe: qiime2/alpha_diversity_multi_canonical.py
# bindable sample (recipe declares only sample_id/habitat; metric cols are dynamic)
fixture: alpha_diversity.tsv
renders_as:
  # code-mode figure: 2×2 facet of the four alpha-diversity metrics by habitat,
  # each panel with its own y-scale (metrics span very different ranges).
  - component: figure
    code: |
      # reshape wide -> long so each metric becomes a facet panel (stays polars)
      df_modified = df.unpivot(
          index=["sample_id", "habitat"],
          on=["shannon", "observed_features", "faith_pd", "evenness"],
          variable_name="metric",
          value_name="value",
      )

      fig = px.box(
          df_modified,
          x="habitat", y="value", color="habitat",
          facet_col="metric", facet_col_wrap=2, points="all",
          category_orders={"metric": ["shannon", "observed_features", "faith_pd", "evenness"]},
          title="Alpha diversity by habitat",
      )

      fig.update_yaxes(matches=None)  # each panel keeps its own scale
      fig.for_each_annotation(lambda a: a.update(text=a.text.split("=")[-1]))
      fig.update_layout(showlegend=True, legend_title_text="habitat", boxmode="group")
  # one Tukey box-plot distribution card per metric (hero average + box-plot strip)
  - { component: card, column: shannon,           aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: observed_features, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: faith_pd,          aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: evenness,          aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: table }

outputs.name: Relative abundance
outputs.rawYaml:
id: qiime2_rel_abundance
name: Relative abundance
mode: rel-abundance
description: Per-sample relative-abundance table with taxonomy ranks.
nf_core_url: https://github.com/nf-core/modules/tree/master/modules/nf-core/qiime2/relativeabundancetables
find: { path_glob: "**/qiime2/rel_abundance_tables/rel-table-*.tsv" }
recipe: nf-core/ampliseq/taxonomy_rel_abundance.py
fixture: rel_abundance.tsv
renders_as:
  # wide per-rank columns (Kingdom/Phylum) → sunburst fits; stacked_taxonomy
  # needs a single long-format rank column this table lacks.
  #
  # No complex_heatmap here: this table is long (one row per sample × taxon) and
  # the server's heatmap reads a wide matrix off `index_column` with no pivot
  # step, so it can only ever plot the single `rel_abundance` column. The
  # clustered heatmap is offered by `qiime2_clustered_heatmap`, which binds the
  # canonical taxon × sample matrix the same reshape produces.
  - { id: sunburst, component: advanced_viz, kind: sunburst, roles: {abundance: rel_abundance} }
  # Metric cards and the row-level table behind them: the readings the
  # nf-core dashboards were already computing off this output by hand.
  - { component: card, column: rel_abundance, aggregation: median, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: taxonomy, aggregation: nunique, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: Phylum, top_n_count: 3 }

recipe: qiime2/taxonomy_composition.py

renders_as:
  - { component: figure, visu_type: bar, dict_kwargs: {x: sample, y: count, color: Phylum} }
  - { component: table }

outputs.name: Abundance matrix

id: qiime2_taxonomy_heatmap

  pivoted from the relative-abundance table.

outputs.description: Windowed read depth along the whole reference, from Qualimap BamQC's own coverage_across_reference table. Qualimap reports the window centre on the concatenated reference, so the recipe maps each window back onto its contig using the per-contig lengths in the same run's genome_results.txt; without that file the track falls back to a single pseudo-contig.
outputs.name: Coverage across the reference

outputs.description: How many bases of the reference sit at each read depth, from Qualimap BamQC. The share of the reference at each depth is derived alongside the raw base count so two libraries mapped against different references stay comparable.
outputs.name: Coverage histogram
outputs.rawYaml:
id: qualimap_coverage_histogram
name: Coverage histogram
description: >-
  How many bases of the reference sit at each read depth, from Qualimap BamQC.
  The share of the reference at each depth is derived alongside the raw base
  count so two libraries mapped against different references stay comparable.
find:
  path_glob: "**/coverage_histogram.txt"
recipe: qualimap/coverage_histogram.py
fixture: coverage_histogram.tsv
renders_as:
  - { id: depth_histogram_profile, component: advanced_viz, kind: profile,
      roles: {series: sample, x: coverage, y: fraction} }
  - { component: figure, visu_type: line, dict_kwargs: {x: coverage, y: n_genomic_locations, color: sample, title: Bases of the reference at each depth} }
  - { component: card, column: coverage, aggregation: max, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: sample, top_n_count: 3 }
  - { component: card, column: n_genomic_locations, aggregation: sum, secondary_layout: donut, breakdown_col: sample }
  - { component: table, page_size: 25 }

dict_kwargs.title: Bases of the reference at each depth

outputs.description: Per-contig length, mapped bases and mean depth from the last block of Qualimap BamQC's genome_results.txt, plus the depth relative to the library's own genome-wide mean. The substrate of a coverage-ratio sex call and the quickest read on whether one scaffold soaked up the library.
outputs.name: Coverage per contig

dict_kwargs.title: Depth per contig, relative to the library mean

outputs.description: The share of the reference covered at least X deep, from Qualimap BamQC. The number a shallow shotgun library is judged on, because a mean depth well under 1X says nothing about whether the reads are spread over the genome or piled on a tenth of it.
outputs.name: Genome fraction by depth
outputs.rawYaml:
id: qualimap_genome_fraction_coverage
name: Genome fraction by depth
description: >-
  The share of the reference covered at least X deep, from Qualimap BamQC. The
  number a shallow shotgun library is judged on, because a mean depth well
  under 1X says nothing about whether the reads are spread over the genome or
  piled on a tenth of it.
find:
  path_glob: "**/genome_fraction_coverage.txt"
recipe: qualimap/genome_fraction_coverage.py
fixture: genome_fraction_coverage.tsv
renders_as:
  - { id: genome_fraction_profile, component: advanced_viz, kind: profile,
      roles: {series: sample, x: min_coverage, y: genome_fraction_pct} }
  - { component: figure, visu_type: line, dict_kwargs: {x: min_coverage, y: genome_fraction_pct, color: sample, title: Share of the reference covered at least X deep} }
  - { component: card, column: genome_fraction_pct, aggregation: max, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: sample, top_n_count: 3 }
  - { component: card, column: genome_fraction_pct, aggregation: average, aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: table, page_size: 25 }

dict_kwargs.title: Share of the reference covered at least X deep

tools.description: Reference-free assembly quality statistics for whole assemblies and for individual bins.
tools.name: QUAST

outputs.description: Contig counts, N50 and assembled length for each assembly, one row per assembler and sample. Total length says how much of the community was assembled at all; N50 says whether that length sits in a few long contigs a binner can work with, or in a drift of short ones it cannot.
outputs.name: Assembly statistics
outputs.rawYaml:
id: quast_assembly_report
name: Assembly statistics
mode: assembly-report
description: >-
  Contig counts, N50 and assembled length for each assembly, one row per
  assembler and sample. Total length says how much of the community was
  assembled at all; N50 says whether that length sits in a few long contigs a
  binner can work with, or in a drift of short ones it cannot.
find:
  path_glob: "**/QUAST/transposed_report.tsv"
  path_glob_alt:
    - "**/quast/transposed_report.tsv"
    - "**/QUAST/*/transposed_report.tsv"
recipe: quast/assembly_report.py
fixture: assembly_report.tsv
renders_as:
  - { id: n50_vs_length, component: advanced_viz, kind: scatter_xy,
      roles: {x: total_length, y: n50, label: assembly_id, color: assembler, size: n_contigs} }
  - { component: figure, visu_type: bar, dict_kwargs: {x: assembly_id, y: total_length, color: assembler, title: Assembled length per assembly} }
  - { component: figure, visu_type: bar, dict_kwargs: {x: assembler, y: n50, color: sample, title: Contig N50 by assembler} }
  - { component: card, column: total_length, aggregation: sum,
      secondary_layout: composition, breakdown_col: assembler }
  - { component: card, column: n50, aggregation: median,
      aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: card, column: n_contigs, aggregation: sum,
      secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: assembly_id, top_n_count: 5 }
  - { component: card, column: largest_contig, aggregation: max,
      secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: assembler, top_n_count: 4 }
  - { component: card, column: gc_percent, aggregation: average,
      aggregations: [box_plot_stats], secondary_layout: box_plot }
  - { component: table }

  explicitly, which makes the composition sum to one.

recipe: rseqc/read_distribution.py

renders_as:
  # Two resolutions in one tile: the coarse region classes, or the individual
  # RSeQC features, picked with the rank filter.
  - id: distribution_composition
    component: advanced_viz
    kind: stacked_taxonomy
    roles: { sample_id: sample_id, taxon: taxon, rank: rank, abundance: abundance }
  # The frame carries both resolutions, so a card that SUMS tag_count would add
  # the region-class rows to the feature rows they are made of and report twice
  # the library. Counting distinct annotation names per class is rank-safe.
  - {
      component: card,
      column: taxon,
      aggregation: nunique,
      secondary_layout: top_n,
      breakdown_col: region_class,
      top_n_count: 5,
    }
  - { component: table }

outputs.name: Cross-profiler lineages
outputs.rawYaml:
id: taxpasta_lineage
name: Cross-profiler lineages
mode: merge/lineage
description: >-
  The same grain as the cross-profiler abundances, with the seven NCBI ranks widened
  into their own columns so a hierarchy can be drawn from them. The ancestry is read
  back out of the indented kraken-style reports the run writes, and reads no
  profiler could place keep an explicit unclassified lineage rather than dropping
  out of the rings.
nf_core_url: https://github.com/nf-core/modules/tree/master/modules/nf-core/taxpasta/merge
find: { path_glob: "**/taxpasta/*.tsv" }
recipe: taxpasta/lineage.py
fixture: lineage.tsv
renders_as:
  # Wide per-rank columns -> sunburst, exactly the shape melon's pooled table has,
  # except this one keeps the profiler, database and sample it came from.
  - {
      id: lineage_sunburst,
      component: advanced_viz,
      kind: sunburst,
      roles:
        {
          ranks: [superkingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species],
          abundance: rel_abundance,
        },
    }
  # Pavian's flow view: the root fans out into the domains, and the reads the
  # profiler could not place leave it as their own branch. `steps` is the catalog
  # spelling of the tile's `step_cols`; a dashboard widens or narrows it.
  - {
      id: lineage_sankey,
      component: advanced_viz,
      kind: sankey,
      roles: { steps: [root, superkingdom, phylum, genus] },
    }
  - {
      component: card,
      column: species,
      aggregation: nunique,
      secondary_layout: top_n,
      breakdown_col: phylum,
      top_n_count: 4,
    }
  - {
      component: card,
      column: rel_abundance,
      aggregation: median,
      aggregations: [box_plot_stats],
      secondary_layout: box_plot,
    }
  - {
      component: card,
      column: phylum,
      aggregation: nunique,
      secondary_layout: composition,
      breakdown_col: superkingdom,
    }
  - {
      component: card,
      column: rel_abundance,
      aggregation: max,
      secondary_layout: gauge,
      coverage_max: 1,
    }
  - { component: interactive, interactive_type: MultiSelect, column_name: superkingdom }
  - { component: interactive, interactive_type: MultiSelect, column_name: phylum }
  - { component: table }

name: Taxon by run matrix
mode: merge/matrix
description: >-
  The top taxa as a wide taxon by profiling-run matrix of relative abundances,
  with the taxonomic rank as a row annotation and the profiler and platform of
  each column serialised for the heatmap's column strips.
nf_core_url: https://github.com/nf-core/modules/tree/master/modules/nf-core/taxpasta/merge
find: { path_glob: "**/taxpasta/*.tsv" }
recipe: taxpasta/matrix.py
fixture: matrix.tsv
renders_as:
  - {
      id: concordance_heatmap,
      component: advanced_viz,
      kind: complex_heatmap,
      roles: { index: taxon },
    }
  - { component: table }

outputs.name: Profiler detection overlap
outputs.rawYaml:
id: taxpasta_presence
name: Profiler detection overlap
mode: merge/presence
description: >-
  Per sample and taxon, a 0/1 membership column for every profiler in the run.
  The intersections show how much of the community the classifiers agree on and
  how long each profiler's private tail is.
nf_core_url: https://github.com/nf-core/modules/tree/master/modules/nf-core/taxpasta/merge
find: { path_glob: "**/taxpasta/*.tsv" }
recipe: taxpasta/presence.py
fixture: presence.tsv
renders_as:
  # upset_plot binds no canonical role: the set columns are the run's profilers,
  # so they are named in the tile's config rather than in a role.
  - { id: profiler_upset, component: advanced_viz, kind: upset_plot }
  - {
      component: card,
      column: n_profilers,
      aggregation: median,
      aggregations: [box_plot_stats],
      secondary_layout: box_plot,
    }
  - { component: table }
  # Metric cards and the row-level table behind them: the readings the
  # nf-core dashboards were already computing off this output by hand.
  - { component: card, column: taxon, aggregation: nunique, secondary_layout: top_n, breakdown_col: rank, top_n_count: 4 }
  - { component: card, column: n_profilers, aggregation: max, secondary_layout: gauge, coverage_max: 12 }
